clue.text: Caribbean island with land inside on top of everything

indicators.note: inside says the word for land sits within the phrase for on top of everything

parts.note: on top of everything means as well, too
to land a fish or a prize is to bag it

explanation.surface: A geography note about an island with land in the middle and something extra on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On top of everything' looks like a position, but it means 'in addition'; 'land' is the verb, as when landing a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is the smaller island of the Caribbean nation Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Petty criminal pockets endless money, acting predictably

indicators.note: pockets means the scrambled word takes the other piece inside it
criminal suggests the letters of petty are misused and reordered
endless means the word for money loses its last letter

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: A small-time crook pockets some cash, behaving as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petty criminal' reads as one crook, but 'criminal' is the anagram signal on PETTY, making TYPET; 'endless' trims the money word before 'pockets' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor stuck in one kind of role plays the same part predictably.

clue.text: Prevent cricket side being noble

parts.note: to bar is to prevent
the on side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team kept from being high-born.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the nobility, the lowest rank of peer in Britain.

clue.text: Talk idly and hang up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to sag is to hang down loosely

explanation.surface: Someone chatting idly and then ending the phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hang up' looks like ending a call, but 'up' is the reversal of SAG.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is British slang for chattering idly at length.

clue.text: Stress while in US city, losing head

indicators.note: in says the word for while is placed inside the trimmed city
losing head means the city's first letter is dropped

parts.note: Memphis is a city in Tennessee
as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'

explanation.surface: Someone under strain while visiting an American city, losing their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the city's first letter, leaving EMPHIS; 'in' then splits it after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress laid on a word or point is emphasis, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Rob drinks to appear a fool

parts.note: to mug is to rob in the street
gins are drinks

explanation.surface: Robbing someone of their drinks makes you look silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear' is a link; the answer is British slang for a dupe, often oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggins is British slang for a gullible person, often used of oneself.

clue.text: Murmur about a curious mark, rash

indicators.note: about says the word for murmur goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to hum is to murmur
rum is British slang for curious or odd
a scar is a mark

explanation.surface: Someone mutters about an odd mark, acting rashly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the murmur word is split around the rest; 'rum' meaning odd is old-fashioned British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated phrase describes reckless, impetuous behaviour, the same as rash.

clue.text: Bitterly sliced in two by the wind

indicators.note: sliced in two by says the word for bitterly is split with the other word inside

parts.note: sourly means bitterly

explanation.surface: Someone cut in two by a bitter wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like part of the surface's weather picture but is the definition, a noun; 'sliced in two by' splits the bitter word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a southerly is a wind blowing from the south.

clue.text: Transport requires trickery when short of time

indicators.note: when short of says a letter is taken out of the word for trickery

parts.note: sleight is cunning or trickery, as in sleight of hand

explanation.surface: Getting a vehicle needs some trickery when time is short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' is a link; SLEIGHT loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge pulled by horses or reindeer is a form of transport.

clue.text: Galley served some lamb, I remember

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner recalls the galley serving up some lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'served', but a bireme is simply a galley; 'served' is a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme was an ancient galley with two banks of oars.

clue.text: Damn cold!

explanation.surface: An exclamation about freezing weather.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang this word is a mild intensifier ('a perishing nuisance'), and it also means bitterly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are British colloquial: an intensifying curse word and a description of freezing weather.

clue.text: Pretty girl capturing nun's heart creates stir

indicators.note: capturing says the girl's name holds the middle letter of nun

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name, and a rose suggests prettiness

indicators.note: heart picks the central letter of the word nun

explanation.surface: An attractive young woman who takes in a nun causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creates' is a link here; the middle letter U of 'nun' goes inside ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone or something is to stir it into action, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Protection for buyers with poor incomes -—- right sum needed

indicators.note: poor suggests the following letters are in bad shape and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A complaint that consumer protection is needed because poor people's incomes need the right sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' looks like it describes the incomes, but it signals the anagram of INCOMES + R + SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumerism also means the movement protecting shoppers' interests, as with consumer rights campaigns.

clue.text: Fixed wings are cool!

explanation.surface: An enthusiast praising fixed-wing aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Wings that are fixed cannot be flapped, which is the cryptic reading; the plain sense is calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never loses their composure is cool, calm under pressure.

clue.text: Sympathetic gesture offered when jumbo unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: jumbo, as an adjective, means huge

explanation.surface: A kind gesture offered when an elephant is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests an elephant or a jet, but it is the adjective, HUGE, losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrace is a sympathetic gesture offered to comfort someone.

clue.text: Those following fairies about a bit?

indicators.note: about here means turned around, each piece read backwards in its place

parts.note: fans are followers of a team or star
an elf is a kind of fairy

explanation.surface: A question about whether fairy followers are about a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns both FANS and ELF in place, giving SNAF + FLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A snaffle is a simple jointed bit used in a horse's mouth; the question mark flags the horsey sense.

clue.text: Adjacent, description of hypotenuse?

explanation.surface: A geometry note about triangle sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right-angled triangle, so it is literally 'a long side'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adjacent means next to something, side by side.

clue.text: Rescue should be organised, fast

indicators.note: should be organised says the letters of the preceding word are to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: A demand that a rescue be organised quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like 'quickly' but means firmly fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held fast is firmly fixed, which is a sense of secure.

clue.text: Perceptive faculty certainly cutting a figure

indicators.note: cutting says the word for certainly slices into the figure

parts.note: eight is a figure, a number
yes means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone sharp-witted certainly cuts a fine figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting a figure' reads as an idiom for looking impressive, but 'cutting' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The faculty of seeing is the most obvious of the perceptive senses.

clue.text: Austrian behind bars in back half of prison, with order returned

indicators.note: returned says the letters gathered are read backwards
back half of keeps only the second half of the prison's name

parts.note: Alcatraz was the island prison in San Francisco Bay
OM stands for the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: An Austrian locked up in a jail, with orders sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind bars' suggests prison, but the composer is behind the bars of music. TRAZ (back half of ALCATRAZ) plus OM, all reversed by 'returned'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer wrote countless bars of music, so he is cryptically the one behind them.

clue.text: Gate where spiv keeps pot

indicators.note: keeps says the word for spiv holds the vessel inside it

parts.note: a tout is a spiv, a seller of tickets on the street
an urn is a pot

explanation.surface: A ticket gate where a shady dealer hangs on to the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gate' means the attendance at a match, not a door; a spiv is British slang for a flashy petty dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports gate is the number attending, which is the same as the attendance figure.

clue.text: Shrine to fit round place where criminals would hang, not burn

indicators.note: round says the word for fit goes around the shortened place name

parts.note: to marry two parts is to fit them together

indicators.note: not says the word burn is removed from the place name

parts.note: Tyburn was London's main gallows site for centuries
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shrine adapted to stand at the old gallows, where criminals were hanged rather than burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyburn was London's gallows near today's Marble Arch; 'not burn' strips the last four letters, and 'round' puts the fit word around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyry is a shrine or chapel built in honour of a martyr.

clue.text: Girl needing help, besieged by chaps

indicators.note: besieged by says the help is surrounded by the chaps

parts.note: chaps are men
aid is help

explanation.surface: A damsel in distress surrounded by men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old-fashioned word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Virtually immobile company which will go to the wall?

definitions.text: which will go to the wall?

indicators.note: virtually means almost all of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: stuck means immobile

explanation.surface: A nearly paralysed firm that is likely to go bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to the wall' suggests bankruptcy, but the plaster literally goes on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is plaster applied to walls, so it is what goes on the wall.

clue.text: Pull when heavy, less hard

indicators.note: less says a letter is taken away from the word for heavy

parts.note: a heavy is a thug, a hired tough
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A heavy pull, a little less hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a heavy is a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: To tug is to pull sharply, a direct synonym.

clue.text: About to catch Irishman in underwear, calling for the authorities

indicators.note: in says the combined piece goes into the underwear

parts.note: pants are underwear

indicators.note: to catch says the word for about holds the man's name

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Liam is a typically Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An embarrassing arrest of an Irishman in his underpants, with the police being called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling for' is a link meaning 'required by'; 'to catch' and 'in' make a container within a container.
explanation.definitionFit: National legislatures are governing bodies, so parliaments are the authorities.

clue.text: Something which might run around one row

indicators.note: around says the runny thing goes round the one

parts.note: a nose runs with a cold
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone running around a single line of seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a line, but it is a din (rhymes with cow).
explanation.definitionFit: A row, in the sense of a racket or din, is noise.

clue.text: Celsius? You might be out on this scale

parts.words: You might be out on this
parts.note: to be out on a limb is to be in an exposed position

explanation.surface: A question about the Celsius temperature scale and being out on a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' suggests a temperature scale beside Celsius, but it is the verb, to go up.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or peak is to climb it, a synonym.

clue.text: One captivated by very long novel that's topping

indicators.note: captivated by says the one is held inside the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters of very long are made anew

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone enthralled by a very long novel they consider excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' turns VERY LONG into OVERLYNG; I goes inside before the final NG.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying over something is to top it, so the word means topping in that literal sense.

clue.text: Shelter from wintry weather, way being invisible

indicators.note: being invisible says the way disappears from the weather word

parts.note: sleet is wintry weather
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Taking shelter from the wintry weather when the road cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link; SLEET loses S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee is the side sheltered from the wind, so it is shelter.

clue.text: Exaggerated about father abroad getting a little light work

indicators.note: about says the word for exaggerated surrounds the foreign father

parts.note: OTT is over the top, exaggerated
pere is French for father

explanation.surface: An overdone account of a father overseas getting a bit of light work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link; 'father abroad' signals the French word, and 'little' is part of the definition, since an operetta is a small opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short light opera, literally a little opera.

clue.text: Choose second, choose again

parts.note: the word choose appears again, here meaning elect

explanation.surface: An instruction to choose second and then choose again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' marks the clue's second 'choose', which gives ELECT after S.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to choose, a direct synonym.
